title: Clear the Streets. Reclaim Our Neighborhoods Press Conference 8/6/26
description:
Abandoned and inoperable vehicles can create safety hazards, attract illegal dumping, and contribute to neighborhood blight. Now, Los Angeles City Council District 9 and the Los Angeles Department of Transportation are launching “Clear the Streets: Reclaim Our Neighborhoods,” a new campaign designed to help South LA residents identify and report problem vehicles.

The campaign will use billboards, posters, social media, and other educational materials to explain which vehicles may qualify for removal and how residents can report them. Vehicles may be eligible for enforcement if they have not moved for 72 hours, are inoperable or unregistered, block traffic lanes, sidewalks, fire hydrants or driveways, or pose a public or environmental hazard.

During fiscal year 2025–26, LADOT removed 6,661 abandoned vehicles from streets across Los Angeles. Through this new partnership, CD9 will work with LADOT, parking enforcement, community organizations, and residents to identify recurring problem areas and improve coordination.

Report an abandoned or inoperable vehicle:

📞 CD9: 213-791-0362
📧 Email: cd9abandon@lacity.org
📞 Citywide hotline: 1-800-ABANDON (1-800-222-6366)
🕗 Monday through Friday, 8 a.m.–5 p.m.
